[[Category:MRI]]
'''Diffusion MRI (dMRI)''' is a [[magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)]] technique measuring the [[Brownian motion]] of $H_2O$ molecules in a medium, including human tissue.

== Application ==

[[File:DMRI water diffusion and tissue structure.png|thumbnail|As explained in ''[[Source:Looking into the functional architecture of the brain with diffusion MRI (Scholarly article)|Le Bihan (2003)]], biological tissues modulate free diffusion, so dMRI results detect tissue microstructure.]]
[[File:Diffusion MRI brain scan.png|thumbnail|Comparison of two dMRI scans at different resolutions of a human brain]]
'''dMRI''' can be employed to model the microstructure of [[biological tissues]].<ref>{{#cite:Q2758}}</ref> It has been identified as particularly useful for mapping white matter routes in the brain for surgical planning.<ref>{{#cite:Q2755}}</ref>
